The fixed point and derivative −1 equations give the stated z_* and K_*, and z_*>ν puts even the last intermediate linear-branch point strictly above the switch. A single nonlinear visit forces primitive period M. Along the nearby fixed-point branch, dρ/dz=−a(1−u)/(1−z)^2<0, dz/dK>0, and dK/dμ<0, so the flip is transverse. Independent composition yields A=−2(b₂²+b₃), B=−b₂A/2. At A=0, set v=2−a and d=1−z_*; in units of d the doubled coefficient is v²(2v−3)(v−3)/405. Dividing by d^4 with d=a(1−2a)/(2(1−a²)) gives the claimed negative quintic. The unique zero lies between 0 and 1/2 by monotonicity and the sign at the endpoints. Reciprocal fourth powers have increments tending to 4κ after local contraction, giving the exact nonfixed-orbit asymptotic. The rational obstruction follows from coprimality of s+r and s after clearing denominators. For the branch proof, one need not assume the displacement quotient is literally a smooth function of h²: center at the parameter-dependent fixed point, choose s=ρ²−1, and solve (P_s²(h)−h)/h=0 for s as a function of h. Its expansion is s=−A h²+O(h³), or s=−C h⁴+O(h⁵) at degeneracy, and it is strictly monotone on each side sufficiently close to 0. This gives two points paired by P_s and the asserted side and stability by differentiating the quotient. The generic repelling escape law follows from reciprocal-square decrements tending to 2A, with only a bounded number of iterates beyond any fixed smaller cutoff. This is local to the specified itinerary and exact recurrence, not a result for a physical flow or all orbits.
